software.distribution_policy: Installed optionally from upstream. No upstream implementation is copied into this adapter. A method citation is not a replacement for required license notices.
software.version_evidence: Official PyPI and stable API documentation checked; both classes executed from the actual 0.0.3 distribution in an isolated test dependency directory. Runtime versions are recorded in each comparison.

methods.citation: Leske S, Dalal SS (2019). Reducing power line noise in EEG and MEG data via spectrum interpolation. NeuroImage 189:763-776.
methods.operation: Upstream SpectrumInterpolation on each supported continuous piece independently, preserving its original time axis.
methods.parameters: Explicit 50 or 60 Hz fundamental, harmonic count limited by Nyquist and reference-band support, default 1 Hz replacement half-width and 2 Hz neighboring reference width.
methods.boundary: Frequency-domain amplitude replacement can remove an overlapping biological component. A reduction in line-frequency power does not identify the removed component as artifact.

methods.citation: de Cheveigne A (2020). ZapLine: A simple and effective method to remove power line artifacts. NeuroImage 207:116356.
methods.operation: Upstream standard ZapLine, with a prospectively fixed component count and adaptive mode disabled, fitted separately within each supported piece.
methods.parameters: Default one removed component; explicit 50 or 60 Hz fundamental and harmonics; nfft represents 4 seconds (minimum 256); reg=1e-9, whiten=false, crossfade=0.
methods.boundary: This is not ZapLine-plus. Fixed component removal can change off-target frequencies and remove genuine signal, including in a line-free control. No automatic best-method choice is made.

methods.operation: Loads the shipped PRAYCG recipe and reproduces its numerical bandpass/reference transform for comparison, not the full governed derivative's task, QC, event or artifact-eligibility workflow.
methods.athena_v1_2: Fourth-order Butterworth 1-40 Hz, scipy sosfiltfilt with default odd-reflection padding, native acquisition reference, no notch.
methods.standard_v0_1: Shipped standard recipe: fourth-order Butterworth 1-45 Hz, optional configured Q=30 notch (currently null), average reference of nonflat retained channels. Preview channel retention is assessed within each selected support piece, not over a separate governed protocol window.
methods.boundary: Bandpass/reference changes and line suppression are different operations. Candidate line suppressors operate on original data, not on already-bandlimited current output. This is intentionally displayed rather than hidden in a single improvement score.

evidence_rules.units: Explicit voltage units converted to microvolts, with per-channel conversion factors retained. Unknown units are not inferred.
evidence_rules.timing: Original seconds and sample indices retained. Unsupported timing, NaNs, user exclusions and declared boundaries are never bridged. No resampling, interpolation of missing samples, or clock repair.
evidence_rules.support: Independent pieces, at least 16 seconds by default, five-second edge guards on each side. Whole-segment retrospective support is disclosed; guards are not a proof of finite impulse support.
evidence_rules.difference: Original minus transformed includes any signal removed, not only noise.
evidence_rules.spectra: Four-second Hann Welch estimates, 50% overlap, constant detrend, density scaling. Piece-specific estimates pooled by actual Welch-window count; temporal gaps never concatenated.
evidence_rules.controls: Fixed-seed clean, additive-60-Hz and genuine-58-Hz-plus-60-Hz synthetic controls report error against known truth and retained 58-Hz amplitude. These test software behavior, not hardware or physiological validity.
